verdicts.evidence: The local import binds os to the operating-system module, and the if condition directly tests os.name (f1:12-13).
The then block executes when os.name equals the literal nt; there is no intervening negation or early exit (f1:13-16).
The condition reads the operating-system family through os.name, so the os category fits (f1:13).
The region has one enclosing conditional, whose sole test is c1; satisfying that one condition reaches the then block (f1:13-16).
The operating-system check enables the execution block, with no alternate payload branch or environment-selected destination (f1:13-18; f2:13-18).
The condition activates execution on the nt operating-system family; it does not test for an analysis environment (f1:13-16).
The check restricts the execution block to the nt operating-system family, while ordinary installation follows outside the condition, supporting targeting (f1:13-18).

The exec call is inside the then region in f1, but the network call is supplied only in derived f2. The packet supplies no checked decode connecting f1's encrypted argument to f2:16, so the complete sink path is unconfirmed.

The visible run method places exec under the operating-system check, and its installation registration provides no visible bypass (f1:11-18; f1:29-31). The encrypted code's connection to the derived network sink remains unchecked, preventing a complete exclusivity finding.

The derived code imports requests and passes fetched response text to exec (f2:14-16), supporting those behaviours within that file. The cited exec sink in f1:16 instead consumes decrypted bytes, and no checked decode establishes that those bytes execute the supplied download code.
